judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the advantage of any other Insured' is terse and its application where a single corporate group holds all interests is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With c074 making every Organization an Insured and c087 sweeping in subsidiaries, the exclusion could be read to defeat intra-group losses that the insuring clauses cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Similar recognized place of safe deposit' and 'any person who is duly authorized ... to have custody' are broad, but the excess proviso limits the effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps with the In Transit definition (c075(b)) which contemplates custody by an authorised person, and with the Other Insurance clause c121, though the excess proviso reconciles them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any authorized representative of an Insured' is undefined and the trailing 'or other fraudulent, dishonest or criminal act' is an open catch-all after a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It could be read to swallow the Insuring Clause 5 and 6 grants (c052, c053) wherever an employee or agent is involved, since the proviso rescues only Insuring Clauses 1 and 9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or other similar representative' closes a list of specific intermediaries with a catch-all, and the awareness triggers use imprecise knowledge language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its awareness test parallels c066's Discovery definition and the 60-day rule in c108, which Endorsement 4 (c132) deletes; those interact but do not contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two crisply drawn categories carving other fraud types out of Premises and In Transit coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Draws clean lines between Insuring Clauses 2/3 and Clauses 4-8, avoiding overlap; consistent with c049 and c050.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As distinct from Robbery' signals a boundary the drafter recognised but did not fully define, and 'other extortion payment' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Schedule of Forms lists a Kidnap/Ransom & Extortion Coverage Section, yet no such section is included in this instrument, leaving the interface unstated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific to registered or coupon obligations; a narrow, determinate exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the Forgery coverage in c051 and the Financial Instrument definition c070 without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 60-day cut-off keyed to when 'an Organization becomes aware', which is a looser standard than the defined Discovery term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 4 (c132) deletes Exclusion 17 in its entirety, so this printed provision is not part of the operative contract at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes loss from forgery of 'any written instrument' subject to two cumulative provisos; the double negative structure is hard to work through.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes precisely what c064's Credit Card Fraud definition and c055's grant cover, so the insuring clause has content only through the provisos.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three near-identical limbs each requiring loss sustained before termination plus Discovery and notice within sixty days; repetitive but determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 19 is amended 'in its entirety' twice — by Endorsement 3 (c127), which drops the 60-day notice regime, and by Endorsement 5 (c134), which restores it — so which version governs is genuinely unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Held by the Organization in any capacity whether or not the Organization is liable' is broad but deliberately so, with two express provisos.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c056 and c088's Client/Insured split; no inconsistency located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Operates by textual substitution ('the words sixty (60) days are deleted'), which is workable but depends entirely on the target text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its amendment of Exclusion 19 assumes the printed c110 wording, yet Endorsement 3 (c127) rewrites Exclusion 19 without any '60 days', leaving the substitution with nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limited to two identified situations with a prior-consent requirement and 'reasonable' costs; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly excepted from exclusion 12(i) (c098) and referenced in the suit-limitation clause c118(b); cross-references are accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains an unqualified automatic-coverage sentence followed by a notice-and-premium condition whose failure voids coverage ab initio; the sequence is severe but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its first paragraph is replaced in its entirety by Endorsement 3 (c128), which changes the trigger to loss Discovered after acquisition, so the printed text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four cumulative conditions plus a limits rule; intricate but each element is specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 3 (c129) deletes Subsection 24 in its entirety, so this provision has been removed while other text (c116) still opens 'Subject to Subsection 24'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Its first sentence limits liability to loss 'sustained ... during the Policy Period' while sub-paragraphs (a)-(j) aggregate acts committed 'before or during the Policy Period', a tension on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It opens 'Subject to Subsection 24', which c129 deletes, and its first paragraph is replaced by c130 with a Discovery-based trigger, so three texts compete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clear anti-stacking sentences; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c116's single-limit rule and with c115's prior-loss limits cap, and with the prior-policy termination clause c036.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the earliest practicable moment' and the odd inventory-comparison proviso invite argument, and the suit-limitation sub-paragraphs are garbled in layout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes 90-day notice a condition precedent, which cannot easily be squared with the excuse in GTC c021 and the prejudice requirement in Endorsement 1 (c039).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A least-of valuation formula with named external price sources and fixed dates; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the general valuation clause c022 for this section, which c022 expressly permits, and keys valuation to Discovery consistently with c066.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ranked four-tier waterfall with a clear reinsurance carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with the subrogation clause c023 and the excess provisos in c102 and c121.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Null and void to the extent of the amount recoverable or received' is strong language partly retracted by the following proviso, and 'valid and collectible' is standard but litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the excess proviso in exclusion 12(m) (c102) and with c115's prior-policy limits rule, all pointing to excess treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise substitution of subparagraph (a) adding 'trustee'; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the printed c069(a), so the policy as issued contains two versions of the Executive definition, though the endorsement plainly controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate about headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c038 and the identical formulas in the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion of a specifically identified exclusion; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes c091 from the contract while c125 substitutes a much broader data-related exclusion, so the printed policy and the endorsement must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any similar type of nonpublic information' follows a long specific list in all three limbs, and 'loss involving the disclosure ... or use' is broad enough to reach losses far beyond data breaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its proviso rescues only Insuring Clause 6, so it can be argued to eliminate the Insuring Clause 5 computer-fraud grant (c052) in any fraud involving misused information — a genuine whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headings and unchanged-terms boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated identically across endorsements; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substituted Exclusion 19 is short and internally consistent, requiring loss sustained and Discovered before termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 (c134), bearing the same effective date, also amends Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' to a different text that reinstates 60-day post-termination discovery and notice; the two cannot both stand.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Replacement text is clear: coverage for acquisitions applies to loss Discovered after the acquisition date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the first paragraph of c114 but leaves the balance of Subsection 23 (notice, additional premium, voiding) in place, which is coherent though it must be pieced together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any and all references to Subsection 24 are deleted in their entirety' is a sweeping instruction whose effect on the sentences containing those references is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c116 opens 'Subject to Subsection 24 Liability for Prior Losses', and c036 addresses prior bonds, so deleting the subsection and its references leaves the treatment of prior losses to be reconstructed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substituted sentence is short and definite: loss sustained before termination and Discovered during the Policy Period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with Exclusion 19 as restored by Endorsement 5 (c134), which contemplates Discovery and notice up to sixty days after termination, and with the printed c116 trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate on headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'all other terms remain unchanged' formula is what makes the competing Exclusion 19 amendments hard to rank, but this sentence itself is standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion identifying the target exclusion precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes c108 from the policy, so the printed Crime section and the endorsement schedule must be read together to know that Exclusion 17 has no effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings and unchanged-terms boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with identical language elsewhere in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substituted text is workmanlike, though the closing proviso adds 'issued by the Company or by any affiliate of the Company', a qualifier absent from the other versions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' in direct competition with Endorsement 3 (c127) and pulls against the Discovery trigger substituted by c130, an unresolved internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headings and unchanged-terms boilerplate with stray form-number text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'all other terms remain unchanged' formula does not resolve which Exclusion 19 amendment prevails, but the sentence itself creates no conflict.
